## 🔴 Errors / High-Priority Warnings

### 🔴 1. Package version inconsistency — `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`

| Project | Version |
|---|---|
| `ContosoApp.Api` | **8.0.0** |
| `ContosoApp.Core` | **8.0.0** |
| `ContosoApp.Services` | **8.0.1** |

The Services project pins a different patch version than the other two. At restore time NuGet will unify to 8.0.1 (highest wins), but the `.csproj` files disagree about intent. This causes:
- Confusing diffs when someone runs `dotnet outdated` or Dependabot
- Risk of MSB3277 assembly-version conflicts if a future update touches only some projects

**Fix:** Unify to a single version (8.0.1) — or better, adopt Central Package Management (see 🔵 3 below).

---

### 🔴 2. Test package version skew between test projects

| Package | `Api.Tests` | `Core.Tests` |
|---|---|---|
| `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` | **17.9.0** | **17.10.0** |
| `xunit` | **2.7.1** | **2.8.1** |
| `xunit.runner.visualstudio` | **2.5.6** | **2.8.1** |

Two test projects use materially different major/minor versions of the test infrastructure. This can cause:
- Inconsistent test behavior (xunit 2.7 vs 2.8 has breaking changes in assertion APIs)
- One test project silently using an older, potentially buggy test SDK

**Fix:** Align to the latest version across both projects. Central Package Management eliminates this class of drift entirely.

---

### 🔴 3. Duplicated properties across all 5 projects (consolidation needed)

These **7 properties** are copy-pasted identically into every single project:

```xml
<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

And this property appears in all 3 src projects:

```xml
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

This is a maintenance hazard — upgrading `TargetFramework` to `net9.0` requires editing 5 files and hoping nobody misses one.

**Fix:** Create a `Directory.Build.props` at the repo root (see 🔵 1).

---

### 🔴 4. Duplicated `PrintBuildInfo` target in all 3 src projects

The identical target appears in `Api.csproj`, `Core.csproj`, and `Services.csproj`:

```xml
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
</Target>
```

Duplicated targets are fragile — if you modify the message format in one project, the others diverge silently.

**Fix:** Move to a `Directory.Build.targets` under `src/` (see 🔵 2).

---

## 🟡 Cautions

### 🟡 1. `PrintBuildInfo` target has no `Inputs`/`Outputs`

The custom target runs unconditionally on every build. While `<Message>` is cheap, missing `Inputs`/`Outputs` is an anti-pattern that becomes costly when targets do real work. It also signals to future developers that incrementality doesn't matter here.

**Fix (optional):** Since this target only emits a message, it's acceptable, but add a comment explaining why `Inputs`/`Outputs` are intentionally omitted:

```xml
<!-- Intentionally runs every build: diagnostic message only, no I/O -->
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
```

---

### 🟡 2. Split `PropertyGroup` blocks in src projects

All 3 src projects have two `<PropertyGroup>` blocks — the main one at the top and a second one for `<DocumentationFile>`. While not incorrect, splitting properties across multiple groups without a condition hurts readability.

**Fix:** Merge into a single `<PropertyGroup>` (or consolidate into `Directory.Build.props`).

---

### 🟡 3. `xunit.runner.visualstudio` may need `PrivateAssets="all"`

Test-infrastructure packages like `xunit.runner.visualstudio` are build/test-time only. If any library project ever depends on a test project (e.g., for shared test utilities), the runner package would flow transitively.

```xml
<!-- Recommended -->
<PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" PrivateAssets="all" />
```

Currently `IsPackable=false` on the test projects prevents NuGet packaging, but adding `PrivateAssets` is defensive-in-depth.

---

### 🟡 4. Dual JSON serializers — `System.Text.Json` + `Newtonsoft.Json`

| Project | `System.Text.Json` | `Newtonsoft.Json` |
|---|---|---|
| `ContosoApp.Api` | ✅ 8.0.5 | — |
| `ContosoApp.Core` | ✅ 8.0.5 | — |
| `ContosoApp.Services` | — | ✅ 13.0.3 |

The solution uses two different JSON libraries. This is a common source of subtle serialization bugs (different default casing, null handling, etc.) and increases the dependency surface. Consider standardizing on `System.Text.Json` unless Newtonsoft is required for a specific reason.

## 🔵 Suggestions

### 🔵 1. Create `Directory.Build.props` (repo root)

```xml
<!-- /Directory.Build.props -->
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- XML docs for all non-test projects -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(IsPackable)' != 'false'">
    <DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Test project defaults -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

After this, each `.csproj` shrinks to only its unique content (SDK, packages, project references).

---

### 🔵 2. Create `src/Directory.Build.targets`

```xml
<!-- /src/Directory.Build.targets -->
<Project>
  <!-- Import repo-level targets if they exist -->
  <Import Project="$([MSBuild]::GetPathOfFileAbove('Directory.Build.targets', '$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../'))"
          Condition="Exists('$([MSBuild]::GetPathOfFileAbove('Directory.Build.targets', '$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../'))')" />

  <Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
  </Target>
</Project>
```

This removes the duplicated target from all 3 src projects and provides a single place to modify it.

---

### 🔵 3. Adopt Central Package Management (`Directory.Packages.props`)

```xml
<!-- /Directory.Packages.props -->
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Shared -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" Version="8.0.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.5" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Swashbuckle.AspNetCore" Version="6.5.0" />
    <!-- Test -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.10.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.1.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Then each `.csproj` drops the `Version=` attribute:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit" />
```

This **eliminates version drift by design** — the issues in 🔴 1 and 🔴 2 become structurally impossible.

---

### 🔵 4. After consolidation — slimmed-down project files

Here's what `ContosoApp.Core.csproj` would look like after all three suggestions:

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" />

  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Down from 21 lines to 6 — everything else is inherited.
